help.title: Help

desc.overview: How the platform is laid out and how to reach each part.
desc.assistant: Asking, picking an agent and a model, sources, files and voice.
desc.workflows: Automated work — from email drafts to meeting prep; admins can build new ones.
desc.integrations: Connect a Google account — Gmail, Calendar, Meet and Drive — for the assistant and workflows to read.
desc.agents: Focused assistants for specific jobs; pick one, talk to it, or build your own.
desc.echo: Recording with a live transcript, the records list, speakers and search.
desc.management: Members, invitations, member privileges and the organization's identity — for admins.
desc.settings: Workspace, assistant behavior, security and audit logs; names and photo in Profile.

help.githubNote: The platform's code, docs and development history live on GitHub.

overview.step1: Sign in with your email and password; the home page is the Assistant — ask there and the answer arrives in the conversation.
overview.step2: The side rail has three domains: the Assistant, “Echo” for recording and transcribing meetings, and “Management” for the organization's admins.
overview.step3: Under the assistant's menu you will find Workflows, Integrations and Agents; “History” brings back previous conversations.
overview.step4: “Settings” and “Help” sit at the bottom of the rail; “Profile” opens from the avatar menu.
overview.step5: The avatar menu holds theme, calendar and sign-out; the language toggle is in the top bar, and the breadcrumb above each page is the way back.

assistant.step1: Type your question in the center box and press Enter; the answer arrives right in the conversation.
assistant.step2: Pick an agent from the picker beside the box to talk with that focused assistant; the model and the skill are chosen from the same bar.
assistant.step3: “Sources” attaches your own meetings and calls to a question; “Web search” lets the assistant read the live web.
assistant.step4: Attach up to three text files with “Add file”; the microphone button turns your speech into text.
assistant.step5: Under each answer you can copy it, rate it good or bad, or regenerate it; “How this answer was made” shows the tools it used.
assistant.step6: “History” brings back previous conversations; each one can be renamed, archived, or shared with the organization.

workflows.step1: “Workflows” opens from the assistant's menu; each card is one automated job with its own page and its own switch.
workflows.step2: “Draft email replies”: while it is on, your connected inbox is checked and a reply draft is written for new mail — sending always stays with you.
workflows.step3: “Prepare me for meetings”: about half an hour before each calendar meeting, a preparation brief is written into your conversation.
workflows.step4: Each workflow's switch is personal — turning it on or off affects only your own account.
workflows.step5: A workflow's page shows its Process (the trigger and the steps) and its Runs — upcoming and recent.
workflows.step6: Admins can build a new workflow: a trigger — manual, or an event such as a recording starting, a transcript ready, a meeting summarized, mail arriving or a meeting coming up — plus ordered steps such as search, ask the assistant, extract, decide, propose, apply and notify.

integrations.step1: “Integrations” opens from the assistant's menu: Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Meet and Google Drive.
integrations.step2: One Google sign-in covers all four sources; a connection is yours alone, and only you see its content.
integrations.step3: Each connection's page lists the items read from that source — mail, events or files — beside the connection's details.
integrations.step4: The assistant and workflows only read from these sources; drafts the assistant writes wait until you press Send yourself.
integrations.step5: “Disconnect” on a connection's page revokes access — all of that account's sources disconnect together, and you can reconnect whenever you like.

agents.step1: “Agents” opens from the assistant's menu; three ready-made agents ship with the platform: Meetings, Email and Meeting preparation.
agents.step2: Click an agent to start talking with it in the assistant; its workflows and knowledge appear beside the greeting.
agents.step3: An agent's knowledge is the records you can already access — nothing separate is uploaded.
agents.step4: Use “Create” to build a personal agent: persona and instructions, knowledge, workflows and visibility — step by step.
agents.step5: Organization-wide agents are created and edited by admins only; system agents are part of the platform and are not edited here.

echo.step1: In “New record”, pick your microphone and start recording; the live transcript appears on the same page as you speak.
echo.step2: Take notes right there and tick action items as they come up; send an existing file from the upload icon on the same menu row.
echo.step3: Long sessions split automatically into 30-minute parts, uploaded as you go; “Finish & process” hands the record to transcription.
echo.step4: “Records” lists your recordings; each record's page has four sections: the summary, the transcript, actions & decisions, and notes & attachments.
echo.step5: In “Speakers”, keep people and their titles; enroll a voice and that person is recognized automatically in later meetings.
echo.step6: “Search” scans every transcript and summary you can access and takes you to the record it found.

management.step1: “Management” opens from the side rail and belongs to the organization's admins and owner.
management.step2: In “Users”, see the organization's members, assign roles, approve or disable; search and filters work across all names.
management.step3: In “Invitations”, add people with an invitation link — shown exactly once; an invitation can be revoked and reissued.
management.step4: “Member privileges” sets what members and admins may do — each switch limits exactly one ability.
management.step5: In “General”, edit the organization's name and logo, its default language and the speech-recognition glossary.

settings.step1: “Settings” sits at the bottom of the side rail; “Profile” opens from the avatar menu.
settings.step2: “General” shows your workspace's facts; the calendar (Jalali or Gregorian) and the timezone are set right there.
settings.step3: “Assistant” holds the reply language and length and your standing instructions — they travel with every question you ask.
settings.step4: “Security” lists your live sessions — “this device” is marked; a session idle for too long closes automatically.
settings.step5: “Sign-in methods” shows the ways into the platform; “Audit logs” says who did what, and when.
settings.step6: In “Profile”, edit your names, username and photo, change your password, and export your account data.

wf-starter-followups.name: Meeting follow-ups
wf-starter-followups.description: Pulls the topics out of recent meetings and writes one follow-up line for each.

wf-starter-autotag.name: Automatic meeting tagging
wf-starter-autotag.description: After every meeting the topics are drawn from the transcript and proposed as tags — they are saved once you approve them.

wf-starter-mail-reply.name: Email reply drafts
wf-starter-mail-reply.description: Every new email that arrives is read, and if it wants a reply a draft is written for you to review and send.

wf-starter-meeting-title.name: Meeting title suggestion
wf-starter-meeting-title.description: After every meeting a short title is proposed from the transcript — it is saved once you approve it.

wf-starter-decisions-digest.name: Decisions digest
wf-starter-decisions-digest.description: Collects the decisions from recent meeting summaries and writes a short digest.

wf-starter-action-items.name: Action-item sweep
wf-starter-action-items.description: After every meeting the promised tasks are pulled out with their owner and due date, and a follow-up line is written for each.

wf-starter-open-questions.name: Unanswered questions
wf-starter-open-questions.description: After every meeting the questions that stayed unanswered are collected so none of them gets lost.

wf-starter-topic-history.name: Topic history
wf-starter-topic-history.description: Finds the recurring topics across your meeting summaries and tells how each one has moved.

wf-starter-mail-triage.name: Reply-needed detection
wf-starter-mail-triage.description: Every new email is read, and when it wants a human reply you get a short note.

wf-starter-mail-summary.name: New-mail summary
wf-starter-mail-summary.description: Every new email is summarized in two or three lines: what it wants, from whom, by when.

wf-starter-mail-reply-formal.name: Formal reply drafts
wf-starter-mail-reply-formal.description: For emails that want an answer, a draft in a formal register is written — sending always stays yours.

wf-starter-mail-reply-brief.name: Brief acknowledgements
wf-starter-mail-reply-brief.description: For emails that want an answer, a short two-line acknowledgement draft is written: received, being looked at.

wf-starter-mail-meeting-request.name: Meeting-request detection
wf-starter-mail-meeting-request.description: When an email asks for a meeting or an appointment, you get a short note right away.

wf-starter-mail-context.name: Sender & topic history
wf-starter-mail-context.description: For every new email, whatever the meeting summaries hold about its sender or subject is collected.

wf-starter-prep-brief.name: Pre-meeting brief
wf-starter-prep-brief.description: Shortly before every meeting a short brief is built from your records: what happened, what stayed open, what to ask.

wf-starter-prep-people.name: Who you are meeting
wf-starter-prep-people.description: Before every meeting the conversation history with its participants is reviewed: what was said last, and what each person still owes.

wf-starter-prep-questions.name: Suggested questions
wf-starter-prep-questions.description: Before every meeting a few questions are proposed out of the earlier summaries to move the discussion forward.

wf-starter-prep-open-decisions.name: Open items before the meeting
wf-starter-prep-open-decisions.description: Before every meeting the pending decisions and unfinished tasks are listed so the meeting can close them.

wf-starter-prep-related.name: Related records
wf-starter-prep-related.description: Before every meeting the calls and meetings related to it are found and listed.

wf-starter-prep-today.name: Today at a glance
wf-starter-prep-today.description: Whenever you ask, an overview is built from your latest calls: what happened, what is moving, what needs attention.

wf-starter-prep-agenda.name: Next meeting's agenda
wf-starter-prep-agenda.description: After every meeting, the next meeting's agenda is drafted from its decisions and tasks.

wf-starter-sales-debrief.name: Sales call debrief
wf-starter-sales-debrief.description: After each call, a short sales debrief is written: what the customer wants, their concerns, and the next step.

wf-starter-sales-objections.name: Recurring objections
wf-starter-sales-objections.description: Collects recurring customer concerns and objections from recent call summaries — with the answers that worked.

wf-starter-sales-next-steps.name: Customer next steps
wf-starter-sales-next-steps.description: After each call, the promises and next steps are pulled out with their owner and due date.

wf-starter-sales-commitments.name: Promises we made
wf-starter-sales-commitments.description: Whenever you ask, every promise made to customers in recent calls is collected — before it slips.

gateway.title: API gateway
gateway.intro: Any system can push audio in and pull transcripts, summaries and answers out — under the same permission wall you are under. The named connectors further down this page get built on this gateway later.
gateway.adminOnly: This section belongs to organization admins
gateway.adminOnlyNote: Only an admin can create and revoke keys and webhooks. If you need an integration, ask your organization's admin to create a key in your name; that key can do what you can do.
gateway.keysNote: Every key is created in one member's name and can do exactly what that member can do — no more. If that member is disabled, the key stops working the same moment, with no rotation needed.
gateway.actorNotListed: This id is not in the member list:
gateway.actorInactive: This member is disabled; the key does not work.
gateway.revokeBody: Any system using this key is refused from this moment on. The key is not deleted; its record stays with a revocation date, so what existed and when it was withdrawn remains readable. A revoked key never comes back — carrying on means minting a new one.
gateway.nameHint: So you can tell later which system uses it.
gateway.actsAsNote: This key can do exactly what you can do — no more.
gateway.actsAsLabel: Whose name is this key in?
gateway.actsAsSelectHint: The key gets exactly the access this member has. This choice cannot be changed later.
gateway.actsAsPersonNote: This key can do exactly what {name} can do — no more. If {name} is disabled, this key stops working the same moment.
gateway.actsAsSelfNote: This key can do exactly what you can do — no more. If your account is disabled, this key stops working the same moment.
gateway.allowAssistantHint: The assistant spends model tokens, and that costs money. Closed by default: a leaked or runaway key can read transcripts, but it cannot drain a model budget.
gateway.capabilitiesImmutable: A key's capabilities are decided when it is created and never change afterwards. To change them, revoke the key and mint a new one — so the record reads “one credential ended, a different one began”, rather than leaving a key whose meaning depends on when you looked.
gateway.keyOnceBody: The NeurAI platform keeps only a cryptographic fingerprint of the key, so there is no way to show it again. If you close this without saving it somewhere, the only way forward is to revoke it and create a new one.
gateway.keySaved: I have saved the key somewhere safe
gateway.pauseNote: Pausing keeps the webhook and its delivery history; nothing is deleted.

legal.ownershipBody: Audio you record or upload, its transcripts, and everything derived from them belong to your organization. The transcript is the source of truth; derived artifacts are rebuildable and carry their provenance.
legal.accessBody: Every read and write - including every action of the AI assistant - runs under the requesting member’s own permissions, enforced at the database layer. Nobody, including the assistant, can reach content its caller could not.
legal.processingBody: Speech is transcribed and summarized using the model providers your organization’s admin allows. Model providers receive the content needed to perform the requested task and nothing else.
legal.retentionBody: Deleting a call hides it immediately and permanently purges its audio, transcript and derivatives after the retention window. Conversations with the assistant are archived, never silently deleted.
legal.securityBody: Sessions are httpOnly cookies; tokens never transit the browser. Content never appears in logs. Outbound webhooks carry identifiers and status only, signed with your secret.
legal.changesBody: A revision of these terms changes the version date above. The text never changes silently.

tasks.deleteTaskBody: The task and its checklist, comments and history are removed for good. Archive it instead if you may want it back.
tasks.archiveTaskBody: It leaves the board for the archive. Nothing is deleted — bring it back from the Archive view.
tasks.unarchiveBody: It returns to its column on the board.
tasks.event_undone: put the task back to not done
tasks.deleteLabelBody: It comes off every card that wears it. The cards stay; the label is gone for good.
tasks.removeItemBody: This line will be removed from the checklist and cannot be restored.

meetings.title: Meetings
meetings.readFailed: Could not read the meetings just now.
meetings.empty: No meetings yet. Schedule the first one.
meetings.inviteePlaceholder: A name or an email, Enter to add…
meetings.noRecordYet: No record of this meeting yet.
meetings.processingSubtitle: the AI is analyzing the audio
meetings.processingNote: Depending on the audio length this can take a few minutes. You can switch to other tabs — the result appears right here.
meetings.step_upload_sub: Securely transferring the file to the server
meetings.step_extract_sub: Summary, decisions and action items with AI
meetings.newMeetingTaskPlaceholder: A task out of this meeting…
meetings.fileMissing: The bytes never arrived — a gap in the take.
meetings.noNotes: No notes yet. Write the first one.
meetings.noMinutesYet: The minutes are not written yet — they appear when processing finishes.
meetings.deleteNoteBody: The note is removed for good — notes are annotations, and this one will not come back.
meetings.recordGone: The record is no longer readable — it was deleted or purged.
meetings.newMeetingSubtitle: Title and time — add the agenda and invitees later on the meeting page
meetings.descriptionPlaceholder: A short line about the meeting's goal…
meetings.startFailed: The recording could not start — check microphone access.
meetings.modeExplain_upload: Upload mode — record here anyway, or add the audio file from the Echo menu; processing runs the same either way.
meetings.modeExplain_in_person: In person — recorded by this device's own microphone. Step into «حین جلسه» and the recording begins.
meetings.modeExplain_online: Online — the system audio is recorded so both sides of the call land in one record. Step into «حین جلسه» and pick the tab or screen to share.
meetings.notesNeedRecording: Notes attach to the recording — start the meeting first.
meetings.extractionProvenance: AI-generated from the meeting's summary — the transcript beside it is the record.
meetings.extractionSectionAbsent: The summary has no section of this kind for this meeting.
meetings.meetingTasksSubtitle: Action items on the board — extracted from “{title}”; click a card for details
meetings.whiteboardHint: Draw here — scroll to pan, or use the hand tool. The board stays on this device.
meetings.whiteboardLocalNote: The whiteboard is saved on this device only.
meetings.engineBusy: Another recording is already running — finish or discard it first.
meetings.errMicDenied: Microphone access was denied — recording did not start.
meetings.errShareDenied: Screen sharing was cancelled — recording did not start.
meetings.errShareNoAudio: The shared tab carried no audio — share a tab with sound on.
meetings.finishFailed: Finishing the recording failed — the audio is still on this device. Try again.
meetings.linkFailedRetrying: Linking the record to this meeting failed — retrying.
meetings.noSpeechTitle: The meeting was recorded, but no speech was found
meetings.noSpeechBody: The recording finished and plays back, but the transcriber found no words — usually a muted microphone, or nobody spoke. You can upload a better file to process instead.
meetings.assistantScope: Answers only from this meeting's record
meetings.assistantGreeting: Hello 👋 Ask me about “{title}” — the summary, the tasks, the decisions, who said what, and the follow-ups.
meetings.assistantFailed: The assistant could not answer just now.
meetings.askTasks: Which tasks came out of this meeting?
meetings.noSlides: No presentation loaded — pick a PDF to show it here.
meetings.pdfUnsupported: This browser cannot display the PDF inline.
meetings.deleteMeetingBody: The meeting and its plan go for good. The recording it produced, if any, stays — it is a separate record with its own history.
meetings.roomOnOurServer: The video runs on the platform's own room — nothing is shared with a public service.
meetings.stageSealed: This meeting has a record — the plan and the live stage are closed.
meetings.roomLoadFailed: The video room could not load here. It still opens in a window.
meetings.videoNotConfigured: Video is not set up on this platform yet. An administrator adds the LiveKit keys once, and every meeting gets a room.
meetings.joinHint: Enter a name for others to see.
meetings.joinRefused: This link is no longer valid.
meetings.guestLinkCopied: Guest link copied — any earlier link no longer works.
meetings.guestLinkFailed: The guest link could not be created.
meetings.inviteHint: Pick colleagues, or write anyone else's address.
meetings.attachmentsEmpty: No files have been attached yet.
meetings.itemEmpty_decision: No decisions recorded yet. Write one yourself, or let the assistant add them once the audio is processed.
meetings.itemEmpty_action: No action items recorded yet. Write one yourself, or let the assistant add them once the audio is processed.
meetings.itemEmpty_question: No open questions recorded yet. Write one yourself, or let the assistant add them once the audio is processed.
meetings.itemEmpty_risk: No risks recorded yet. Write one yourself, or let the assistant add them once the audio is processed.
meetings.itemEmpty_entity: No entities recorded yet. Write one yourself, or let the assistant add them once the audio is processed.
meetings.attachmentRemoveBody: This file will be removed from the meeting and cannot be restored.

rooms.bounded: They have gone as far as they can on their own — say something to continue.
rooms.empty: No rooms yet. Open one and call the agents into it.
rooms.noAgents: No agents are available to you.
rooms.openFailed: The room was not opened. Check the title and the agents you picked.
rooms.pickHint: Up to {max} agents in one room. Each gets a turn, and they can hand work to each other.
rooms.roomTitleHint: What are you working out? This becomes the room's name.
rooms.threadEmpty: Say something to begin — the agents answer in turn.
rooms.transportFailed: The connection dropped before the room finished. What was written is still there.
rooms.turnFailed: {name} had nothing to say this turn.
